summary: This note is a Wikipedia infobox-style extract about the United States National Guard, a dual state-federal reserve force of the U.S. Army and Air Force. It records its origins as English colonial militias, its size of about 450,100 personnel, its garrison locations, nicknames, motto, and its commander, the Chief of the National Guard Bureau, General Joseph L. Lengyel, USAF. The content is mostly metadata rather than narrative history.
one_line: Overview of the United States National Guard, a dual state-federal reserve force of the Army and Air Force with about 450,100 personnel.
key_facts: The National Guard of the United States traces its origins to English colonial government militias, dating from December 13, 1636.
The National Guard has been known as "National Guard" since 1824 in New York and since 1903 nationwide.
The National Guard became a dual state-federal reserve force in 1933.
The National Guard operates under federal authority at 10 U.S.C. § E and under state and territorial authority at 32 U.S.C.
The National Guard is a branch of both the United States Army and the United States Air Force.
The National Guard's role is described as the reserve component of the U.S. Armed Forces and the militia of the United States.
The National Guard's size is listed as 450,100 personnel.
The National Guard is part of the National Guard Bureau.
The National Guard's garrison and headquarters span all 50 U.S. states, organized U.S. territories, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and the District of Columbia.
The Army National Guard is nicknamed "Army Guard" and the Air National Guard is nicknamed "Air Guard."
The National Guard's motto is "Always Ready, Always There!"
The Chief of the National Guard Bureau is listed as the commander, currently General Joseph L. Lengyel, USAF.
The note includes seals of the Army National Guard and the Air National Guard as insignia.
